Appreciate the quick answers, Alex — that traffic split helps a lot. A few notes on how Redwood would approach this and options to meet the EU residency requirement: 

1) Regional routing model (recommended):
   - Geo-routing at the edge: route based on client IP / configured region preference to the nearest regional pool.
   - EU pinning / hard-residency option: traffic originating from EU can be pinned to EU-only Dedicated pools (or Private deployment) so both processing and KV/prefix caches remain in-region.
   - Fallbacks: if EU pool is constrained, we can provide a policy-based fallback (e.g., failover to EU-dedicated spare capacity or to EU-hosted soft-fallback with encrypted-at-rest tokens) — we’ll highlight compliance tradeoffs in the MAP.

2) Performance notes / streaming:
   - For streaming UX we recommend configuring smaller token flush intervals + tokenization-aware batching. This preserves p50 while keeping p95 bounded.
   - If you need sub-200ms p50 in US, we’ll recommend local edge routing + aggressive KV prefix caching for common prompts.

3) Capacity / sizing ask for Aditya: please prepare an initial cost/sizing estimate for:
   - Hosted with EU pinning (hosted model variants pinned to EU region)
   - Dedicated EU pool (reserved GPUs) + hosted global for US/APAC fallback
   - Private (VPC) option if Finova needs on-prem or tenant-isolated networking
4) Proposed next meeting: Tue 6/25 at 10am PT for technical deep dive. Confirmable?

Aditya / Dylan — can you take the sizing action and call out any known tradeoffs for streaming vs batched decode (cost vs latency)?

Thanks —
Marissa
